definitions.gloss: surely; no doubt; I can imagine (how ~ it must be)
definitions.explanation: Used to imagine, with sympathy, the feelings or situation of someone else, usually ending with でしょう, だろう or ことでしょう: さぞ{寒|さむ}かったでしょう, you must have been so cold.

examples.japanese: さぞ⟦{寒|さむ}かった→寒い：00664_samui⟧でしょう。
examples.english: You must have been so cold.

examples.japanese: さぞお⟦{疲|つか}れ→疲れ：03518_tsukare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ことでしょう。

⟦{一人|ひとり}→一人：00630_hitori⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{三人|さんにん}→三人：10978_sannin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{育|そだ}てる→育てる：01235_sodateru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、さぞ⟦{大変|たいへん}→大変：00594_taihen⟧だったろう⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: I imagine it must have been very hard raising three children alone.

notes:
Used about other people's feelings or experiences, not one's own. Common in polite speech, letters and condolences, though さぞ itself also appears in plain speech (さぞ⟦{疲|つか}れた→疲れる：00901_tsukareru⟧だろう).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- さぞ〜でしょう / だろう: it must surely be ~
- さぞ〜ことでしょう: it must surely be ~ (more formal)
- さぞかし: a more emphatic form

WATCH OUT:
- Needs a guessing ending (でしょう, だろう, ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧); さぞ⟦{寒|さむ}い→寒い：00664_samui⟧。 on its own is wrong.
- Not for one's own feelings: say ⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{寒|さむ}かった→寒い：00664_samui⟧, not さぞ⟦{寒|さむ}かった→寒い：00664_samui⟧, about yourself.
